content.title: Phillies finalize Opening Day roster: A look at their decisions and what’s next
content.text: CLEARWATER, Fla. — The Phillies had bullpen and bench roster debates until the penultimate day of spring training, then landed on a 26-man roster that has 11 players who were not with them on Opening Day a year ago.They filled out their bullpen with four lefties, including Kyle Backhus and Tim Mayza. Zach Pop earned a bullpen spot with a decent spring. The Phillies chose Rafael Marchán as their backup catcher, putting Garrett Stubbs in limbo. Dylan Moore, a veteran utilityman, will be on the bench.Orion Kerkering, who has made slow progress from a low-grade hamstring strain last month, will begin the season on the injured list. He will be eligible to return April 7, the 11th game of the season.Those were the final details. The larger decisions had been made before camp opened; the Phillies wanted rookies Andrew Painter and Justin Crawford on the roster. Both had fine springs, making their additions a formality.Crawford, 22, will be starting in center field on Opening Day.“Crawford has done very well for himself,” Phillies president of baseball operations Dave Dombrowski said. “He’s played well in center field. Guys have been happy with him in that regard. So we feel that he’s very comfortable out there. He has contributed from an offensive perspective. Again, he’s going to be ninth in the lineup most of the time. You have to suffer the ups and downs, which happens with young guys. But we like him a lot. He’s meshed well. I think he brings a youthful enthusiasm, which is always great for a team. As does as Painter. (Crawford) can fly. He brings another dimension to our club with a legitimate base stealer. So, he’s had a good camp and he’s earned the spot.”Andrew Painter posted a 2.31 ERA over 11 2/3 innings in spring training.Painter, who turns 23 next month, will start the fifth game of the season.“He has thrown the ball very well this spring,” Dombrowski said. “He’s done a good job for us. He just keeps building on what he has. His velocity has been very good. But more impressive has been his breaking stuff. … So even though he’s a young guy coming up that can throw upper 90s, he can also throw a sweeper, slider and changeup. He’s earned it.” In addition to Crawford, Painter, Moore, Backhus, Mayza and Pop, six others are on an Opening Day roster for the first time as Phillies: Jhoan Duran, Brad Keller, Jonathan Bowlan and Otto Kemp. There are only two bullpen holdovers from the 2025 Opening Day roster: José Alvarado and Tanner Banks.Backhus, who arrived in an offseason trade with the Arizona Diamondbacks, impressed this spring. Pop and Mayza won the final bullpen jobs because they threw more strikes this spring and can go multiple innings. Mayza, according to league sources, signed a new contract that guarantees him $1.75 million in the majors. He agreed to an advance consent clause, which permits the Phillies to remove him from the roster within the first 45 days of the season and forgo the remaining guaranteed money.The Phillies sent Zach McCambley, a Rule 5 draft pick, back to the Miami Marlins. McCambley had command issues all spring. Chase Shugart, who is on the 40-man roster, was among the final cuts. He struck out seven and walked seven in 9 2/3 innings this spring. He’ll go to Triple-A Lehigh Valley.“We think we have quite a bit of depth in the bullpen,” Dombrowski said.The Phillies will add three to their 40-man roster — Crawford, Moore and Mayza — while subtracting McCambley and Stubbs. They’ll be at 39 on the 40-man to begin the season.The club will look to find Stubbs a big-league job in the coming days before designating him for assignment. The Phillies would like to keep him in the organization, and that is likely if no team offers Stubbs a job in the majors. He signed a split contract that pays him $575,000 in the minors. Stubbs must accept an outright assignment to Triple A to retain that salary.If Stubbs goes elsewhere, Dombrowski said René Pinto and Caleb Ricketts are next on the catching depth chart.The initial roster, as always, is temporary. Kerkering should return when eligible. Zack Wheeler will pitch in a minor-league game Monday, join the team for Opening Day in Philadelphia and then could begin an official rehab assignment with an affiliate. Wheeler is targeting a return sometime in April.One of the few unknowns of this spring, the status of top prospect Aidan Miller, remains unsolved. Miller has not yet resumed baseball activities, Dombrowski said. He’s sidelined by back soreness. He continues to work out. He will begin the season on the minor-league injured list.“With what he’s had, we’re just making sure he’s feeling good,” Dombrowski said. “We don’t want to push him too fast and then all of a sudden we go backwards. Backs are a little bit tricky like that.”Your browser does not support the video tag.Phillies’ Opening Day rosterCatchers (2): J.T.
